    drafter

    Drafter: a friendly web framework for students learning Python.

    Drafter turns plain Python functions into interactive websites: routes (functions decorated with @route) take the current state and return a Page of components, and start_server(state) launches the site. This package root re-exports everything a student application needs, so a single from drafter import * provides:

    • The route decorator, start_server, and the Page, Fragment, Update, and Redirect payload types.
    • All page components, from basic content (Text, Header, Image, Table) and form inputs (TextBox, Button, SelectBox) to richer widgets (Map, CurrentLocation, Timer, and the audio family such as Tone, Melody, and Sound).
    • Data value types for route parameters and state: Picture for images, DrafterTextFile/DrafterBinaryFile for uploads, and Photo for camera captures.
    • Styling helpers (bold, change_color, update_style, ...) and site configuration functions (set_website_title, set_website_style, ...).
    • Testing and convenience utilities such as assert_equal, dataclass, and open.

    AddMarkerFunction = Callable[[str], None] module-attribute

    The type of the add_marker helper injected into routes handling Map events: annotate a route parameter named add_marker with this, then call it with an optional label to pin the event's location on the live map (see _make_add_marker).

    PageContent = Union[Content, Sequence[Content]] module-attribute

    Audio(src, controls=True, autoplay=False, loop=False, muted=False, persistent=False, **kwargs) dataclass

    Bases: Component

    Renders an HTML5 audio element for embedding sound content.

    Note that this renders an element in the page. For audio control that plays outside of the page context (e.g., background music), consider using the play_audio function from drafter.media.audio.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description

    Source URL of the audio file.

    autoplay bool

    Whether to autoplay the audio.

    Whether to loop the audio.
    muted bool

    Whether to mute the audio.
    persistent bool

    Whether the audio keeps playing across page transitions.

    The HTML tag name, always 'audio'.

    Initialize audio component.

    		 False
    muted bool

    AudioRecorder(name, max_duration=30000, show=True, on_record=None, on_denied=None, on_error=None, **extra_settings) dataclass

    Bases: Component

    Records microphone audio and submits it with the form.

    Shows a record button; after asking for microphone permission (shared with :class:Microphone), it records until stopped or until max_duration milliseconds pass. The completed recording is kept in a hidden form field (named name) as a data URL, so a route parameter with the same name annotated as :class:Recording receives the converted value. Play a recording back by passing its data_url to :class:Sound.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    name str

    The form field name that will contain the Recording data.
    max_duration int

    Maximum recording length in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds).
    show bool

    Whether to display the recorder UI. Defaults to True.
    on_record UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when a recording completes.
    on_denied UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when microphone permission is denied.
    on_error UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when recording fails.

    Initialize the AudioRecorder component.

    Parameters:

    on_denied UrlOrFunction | None

    Camera(name, width=640, height=480, facing='user', mirror=True, show=True, on_capture=None, on_denied=None, on_error=None, **extra_settings) dataclass

    Bases: Component

    Captures photos from the user's webcam and submits them with the form.

    This component follows the same permission workflow as :class:~drafter.components.geolocation.CurrentLocation: it shows an "Enable camera" prompt, and once permission is granted it displays a live preview with a "Take photo" button. The captured photo is kept in a hidden form field (named name), so a route parameter with the same name receives the converted value: annotate it as :class:~drafter.data.images.Picture (or bytes) to get just the image, or as :class:Photo to get the full envelope including the permission status. Display a photo by passing the Picture (or the Photo's data_url) to :class:~drafter.components.images.Image.

    Visual states: - prompt: Shows "Enable camera" button when permission not yet requested - pending: Shows spinner while waiting for permission - live: Shows the live preview with "Take photo" and "Stop" buttons - granted: Shows the captured photo with a "Retake" button - denied: Shows "Camera access denied" message - error: Shows error message if the camera fails - unavailable: Shows message if the camera API is not supported

    After a photo is taken the camera stream is stopped (turning off the camera light); "Retake" starts it again.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    name str

    The form field name that will contain the Photo data.
    width int

    Requested video width in pixels. Defaults to 640.
    height int

    Requested video height in pixels. Defaults to 480.
    facing str

    Which camera to prefer: "user" (front/selfie) or "environment" (rear). Defaults to "user".
    mirror bool

    Whether to mirror the live preview horizontally, like a selfie mirror; the captured photo is never mirrored. Defaults to True.
    show bool

    Whether to display the camera UI. Defaults to True.
    on_capture UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when a photo is captured.
    on_denied UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when camera permission is denied.
    on_error UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when the camera fails.

    Initialize the Camera component.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    name str

    The form field name for the Photo data.

    		 required
    width int

    Requested video width in pixels.

    		 640
    height int

    Requested video height in pixels.

    Component

    Base class for all content that can be added to a page. This class is not meant to be used directly, but rather to be subclassed by other classes.

    Components can be turned into HTML by first calling the plan method, which returns a RenderPlan object. The RenderPlan object contains all the information needed to render the component, including its tag name, attributes, children, and any associated assets.

    Components can be converted to a string using repr, which should be able to roundtrip back to the same component using eval.

    Conceptually, there are three "versions" of the data for the Component: - The "arguments" which are essentially defined by the init method and include both the positional and keyword arguments. These are stored as fields on the Component instance as "internals". The arguments can be either positional, variable, keyword, or extra (kwargs). Every component must have extra_settings, and that ends up as a field as well. When the repr is called, it should generate these arguments to create a string that can be eval'd back into the same component. - The "fields" which are the actual fields contained inside of the Component as an instance. These vary completely by the type of component, but can be used to derive both the arguments and the externals. They should roughly align to the arguments, so that the users can modify them after the fact and have the changes be reflected in the arguments and the externals. - The "externals" which are the HTML attributes, children, assets, and other information needed to render the component. These are derived from the internals, but are not stored that way. Instead, they are generated on the fly when the plan method is called, using the get_attributes, get_children, and get_assets methods.

    Args that are marked as "Content" get turned into Children (child content), other args get turned into attributes.

    So basically the canonical data is the fields, and then some of those fields are identified to create the HTML attributes, children, and assets.

    The default for an argument is to be turned into an attribute of the same name, unless it is in the RENAME_ATTRS dict. The KNOWN_ATTRS list is used to force certain arguments to be turned into attributes, even though the default is to turn them into style properties. The DEFAULT_ATTRS dict is used to provide default values for attributes, which can be overridden by the extra_settings.

    Each subclass declares its constructor parameters in the ARGUMENTS class variable, a list of ComponentArgument entries. Each entry records the parameter's name, its kind ("positional", "var", or "keyword" with a default value), whether it represents child content (is_content) rather than an attribute, and whether it represents an event route handler (is_event). Any extra keyword arguments beyond the declared ones are stored in extra_settings and turned into attributes (or styles).

    A special extra case is the arguments parameter, primarily for Link and Button components, but actually usable by any component. This accepts an ArgumentList that will be turned into a special data--drafter-arguments attribute that will have arguments embedded directly on the element, which will then be passed to any events emanating from that element. The obvious use case is for links and buttons, where you want arguments to be passed when the link or button is clicked, but it could also be used for other events. - The arguments parameter can be a single Arguable, a sequence of Arguable objects, a sequence of (name, value) pairs, or a dict of name to value. - The names MUST be valid Python identifiers, and the values can be any JSON-serializable value (but not dataclasses). - The arguments parameter will be turned into a data--drafter-arguments attribute. - The value of the data--drafter-arguments attribute will be a JSON string. - The arguments parameter will usually be stored in the extra_settings dict, but it can also be stored as a field on the component if desired.

    Under any student-facing circumstances, a string value can be used in place of a Component object (in which case we say it is a Content type). However, the Component object allows for more customization and control over the content. Most situations also allow for a list of Content objects (which we call PageContent), which can be used to group multiple pieces of content together.

    __repr__()

    Represent the component as a constructor-style call with its arguments.

    Generate arguments for repr to enable round-trip serialization.

    Get the CSS and JavaScript assets required by this component.

    The default implementation returns None (no assets). Subclasses override this to bundle dedicated stylesheets or scripts with their rendered output.

    get_attributes(context)

    Build the HTML attributes for this component.

    The default implementation starts from DEFAULT_ATTRS, adds each declared non-content argument (renamed via RENAME_ATTRS, skipping keyword arguments still at their default values), folds in extra_settings (converting arguments and on_* event handlers into their data--drafter-* attributes), and finally adds persistence attributes for PERSISTABLE components. Subclasses override this to add or adjust attributes, usually calling super().get_attributes(context) first.

    Parameters:

    The active Renderer, providing rendering state and configuration.

    		 required

    Dictionary mapping HTML attribute names to values.

    Build the child content for this component.

    The default implementation collects the values of the declared arguments marked is_content, flattening var-args arguments and skipping None values. Subclasses override this to construct derived child elements (e.g., option or list-item RenderPlans).

    CurrentLocation(name, show=True, show_coordinates=False, enable_high_accuracy=True, timeout=10000, maximum_age=0, on_locate=None, on_error=None, on_denied=None, on_timeout=None, **extra_settings) dataclass

    Bases: Component

    A form component that requests and displays browser geolocation.

    This component integrates with the browser's Geolocation API to request user permission and provide location data. It handles multiple visual states based on permission status and keeps a hidden form field (named name) updated with the JSON-encoded location, so a route parameter with the same name annotated as :class:Location receives the converted value.

    Visual states: - prompt: Shows "Use my location" button when permission not yet requested - pending: Shows spinner while waiting for permission - denied: Shows "Location access denied" message with help - granted: Shows "Location available" with optional coordinates - error: Shows error message if geolocation fails - unavailable: Shows message if geolocation API not supported

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    name str

    The form field name that will contain location data.
    show bool

    Whether to display the geolocation status UI. Defaults to True.
    show_coordinates bool

    Whether to display latitude/longitude when granted (default: False).
    enable_high_accuracy bool

    Whether to prefer high-accuracy geolocation. Defaults to True.
    timeout int

    Maximum time to wait for a position in milliseconds. Defaults to 10000.
    maximum_age int

    Maximum cached position age in milliseconds. Defaults to 0.
    on_locate UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when a location (or failure) is resolved. Defaults to None.
    on_error UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when geolocation fails for any reason.
    on_denied UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when geolocation permission is denied.
    on_timeout UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when geolocation request times out.

    Initialize the CurrentLocation component.

    Map(name, center=None, zoom=13, markers=None, height=300, persistent=False, on_click=None, on_marker_click=None, on_move=None, **extra_settings) dataclass

    Bases: Component

    An interactive map that students can click, pan, and zoom.

    Renders an OpenStreetMap-based map (via Leaflet). Clicking the map, clicking a marker, or moving the view can each call a route function. The most recent clicked location is also kept in a hidden form field (named name), so a route parameter with the same name annotated as :class:MapLocation receives the converted value on form submission.

    Note that map tiles are loaded from the internet; without a connection the map area shows a placeholder background but interactions still work.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    name str

    The form field name that will contain the last clicked location.
    center MapLocation | None

    Where the map is initially centered: a :class:MapLocation, a (latitude, longitude) pair, or a "lat,lng" string.
    zoom int

    Initial zoom level (2 shows the whole world, 13 a town, 18 a street). Defaults to 13.
    markers list | None

    A list of :class:MapMarker points to display.
    height int

    Height of the map in pixels. Defaults to 300.
    persistent bool

    Whether the live map (including its current pan/zoom) survives page re-renders. Defaults to False.
    on_click UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when the map is clicked; the event provides latitude and longitude.
    on_marker_click UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when a marker is clicked; the event provides latitude, longitude, and label.
    on_move UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call after the map is panned or zoomed; the event provides latitude, longitude, and zoom.

    Initialize the Map component.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    name str

    The form field name for the last clicked location.

    		 required
    center CenterValue

    Initial map center (MapLocation, (lat, lng), or "lat,lng").

    		 None
    zoom int

    Initial zoom level.

    		 13
    markers list | None

    List of MapMarker points to display.

    		 None
    height int

    Height of the map in pixels.

    		 300
    persistent bool

    Whether the live map survives page re-renders.

    		 False
    on_click UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when the map is clicked.

    		 None
    on_marker_click UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when a marker is clicked.

    		 None
    on_move UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call after panning or zooming.

    		 None
    **extra_settings

    Additional HTML attributes.

    		 {}

    MatPlotLibPlot(extra_matplotlib_settings=None, close_automatically=True, **kwargs) dataclass

    Bases: Component

    Renders a Matplotlib figure as an image or SVG element.

    Captures the current Matplotlib figure at the moment the component is created and embeds it as a base64-encoded PNG or inline SVG. Draw the chart first, then create the component.

    Because the figure is captured (and, by default, closed) on creation, the next chart always starts from a blank figure. That holds even when the page is never shown, such as when a unit test calls the route.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    extra_matplotlib_settings dict

    Dict of Matplotlib savefig keyword arguments.
    close_automatically bool

    Whether creating the component closes the figure, so that later plotting starts a new one.
    tag

    The HTML tag name, always 'img'.
    Example

    plt.plot([12, 15, 11, 18]) plt.title("Treats eaten this week") Page(state, [MatPlotLibPlot()])

    Name Type Description Default
    extra_matplotlib_settings

    		 None

    Melody(notes, tempo=120, waveform='sine', volume=0.8, auto_play=False, controls=False, show=True, effects=None, on_note=None, on_finish=None, **extra_settings) dataclass

    Bases: Component

    Plays a sequence of notes at a tempo using the Web Audio API.

    A melody is just a list: each item is a note name like "C4" (played for one beat), a (note, beats) pair like ("C4", 2), or "rest" for silence. Notes are scheduled with sample-accurate Web Audio timing, so melodies stay in rhythm.

    Note

    An on_note handler that returns a full :class:~drafter.Page re-renders the whole page, which stops and resets this melody after its very first note. To react to notes while the melody keeps playing, return an Update (change state only) or a Fragment targeting another element; save full pages for on_finish.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    notes list[NoteValue]

    The notes to play, in order.
    tempo int | float

    Speed in beats per minute. Defaults to 120.
    waveform str

    The shape of the sound wave: "sine", "square", "triangle", or "sawtooth". Defaults to "sine".
    volume float

    Loudness from 0.0 to 1.0. Defaults to 0.8.
    auto_play bool

    Whether to play as soon as the page loads instead of showing a play button. Defaults to False.
    controls bool

    Whether to show play/pause and restart buttons. Defaults to False.
    show bool

    Whether to display the component. Defaults to True. A hidden auto-play component still shows its "Enable sound" prompt while the browser is blocking sound.
    effects list[AudioEffect] | None

    Optional list of effects (like :class:Echo) applied in order.
    on_note UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call as each note starts.
    on_finish UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when the melody finishes.

    Initialize the Melody component.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    notes list[NoteValue]

    List of note names like 'C4', (note, beats) pairs, or 'rest'.

    tempo int | float

    Speed in beats per minute.

    		 120
    waveform str

    "sine", "square", "triangle", or "sawtooth".

    		 'sine'
    volume float

    Loudness from 0.0 to 1.0.

    		 0.8
    auto_play bool

    Whether to play on page load instead of showing a button.

    		 False
    controls bool

    Whether to show play/pause and restart buttons.

    		 False
    show bool

    Whether to display the component.

    		 True

    		 None

    Bases: Component

    HTML5 meter element for showing a value within a known range.

    Unlike ProgressBar (which shows task completion), a meter is a gauge for a measurement like disk usage or a test score. Browsers color the bar based on the low/high/optimum thresholds.

    value float

    The measured value.
    min float | None

    Lower bound of the range (browser default 0).
    max float | None

    Upper bound of the range (browser default 1).
    low float | None

    Upper bound of the "low" portion of the range.
    high float | None

    Lower bound of the "high" portion of the range.
    optimum float | None

    The optimal value within the range.
    tag

    Microphone(name, threshold=0.5, cooldown=1000, rate=0, show=True, visualize='meter', on_loud=None, on_quiet=None, on_level=None, on_denied=None, on_error=None, **extra_settings) dataclass

    Bases: Component

    Monitors live microphone input and reports how loud the room is.

    This component follows the same permission workflow as :class:~drafter.components.geolocation.CurrentLocation: it shows an "Enable microphone" prompt, and once permission is granted it displays a live level meter. It keeps a hidden form field (named name) updated with the latest :class:AudioLevel snapshot, so a route parameter with the same name annotated as :class:AudioLevel receives the converted value on any form submission.

    The on_loud event is the easiest way to react to sound: it fires when the volume crosses threshold (a clap, a shout), and then not again until cooldown milliseconds have passed. Volume is measured as the peak signal level, so brief sounds like claps register at their full loudness.

    Note

    An on_loud/on_quiet/on_level handler that returns a full :class:~drafter.Page re-renders the whole page, briefly resetting this component (it re-enables itself, but the meter and peak_volume restart). For frequent events, prefer returning an Update (change state only) or a Fragment targeting another element.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    name str

    The form field name that will contain the AudioLevel data.
    threshold float

    The loudness (0.0 to 1.0) that counts as "loud". Defaults to 0.5.
    cooldown int

    Minimum milliseconds between on_loud events. Defaults to 1000.
    rate int

    Milliseconds between on_level events, or 0 to never fire them. Defaults to 0.
    show bool

    Whether to display the permission UI and meter. Defaults to True.
    visualize str

    The live display once granted: "meter", "waveform", or "bars". Defaults to "meter".
    on_loud UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when the volume rises past threshold.
    on_quiet UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when the volume falls back below threshold.
    on_level UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call every rate milliseconds with the current volume.
    on_denied UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when microphone permission is denied.
    on_error UrlOrFunction | None

    Function or URL to call when the microphone fails.

    Initialize the Microphone component.

    Name Type Description Default
    name str

    The form field name for the AudioLevel data.

    The loudness (0.0 to 1.0) that counts as "loud".

    		 0.5

    Minimum milliseconds between on_loud events.

    		 1000

    Page(state, content=None, css=None, js=None) dataclass

    Bases: Fragment

    A page is a full-page response that replaces the entire body content.

    Page is a specialized Fragment that uses a default target pointing to the body element. This content has two critical parts:

    • The state, which is the current value of the backend server for this user's session. This is used to restore the state of the page when the user navigates back to it. Typically, this will be a dataclass or a dictionary, but could also be a list, primitive value, or even None.
    • The content, which is a list of strings, numbers, booleans, and components that will be rendered to the user.

    The content of a page can be any combination of strings, numbers, booleans, and components. Strings will be rendered as paragraphs, numbers and booleans will be rendered as their text form, and components will be rendered as their respective HTML. Components should be classes that inherit from drafter.components.PageContent. If the content is not a list, a ValueError will be raised.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    state

    The state of the page. If only one argument is provided, this will default to be None.

    		 required
    content

    The content of the page. Must always be provided as a list of strings, numbers, booleans, and components.

    		 None
    css

    Optional CSS content to inject dynamically when this page is rendered.

    		 None
    js

    Optional JavaScript content to inject dynamically when this page is rendered.

    		 None

    format_target()

    Format the target for history display, omitting the default.

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    str str

    A , target=... snippet, or an empty string when the target is the default body target.

    A captured photo from a :class:Camera component.

    The picture property provides the captured image as a :class:~drafter.data.images.Picture value, which can be stored in state, manipulated, and handed to :class:~drafter.components.images.Image or :class:~drafter.components.files.Download. (The raw data_url also still works directly with those components.)

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    status PhotoStatus

    Current permission/capture state.
    message str | None

    Optional descriptive message about the status.
    data_url str | None

    The captured photo as a PNG data URL (None if nothing has been captured).
    width int | None

    Width of the captured photo in pixels (None if unavailable).
    height int | None

    Height of the captured photo in pixels (None if unavailable).

    picture property

    The captured photo as a Picture value, or None.

    Lazily decoded from data_url (and cached); None when nothing has been captured (check status/message for why).

    Picture(source, filename=None, mime_type=None)

    An image value: pixels plus optional file metadata.

    A Picture can be built from a path, URL, or data URL string; raw bytes; a PIL image; an uploaded file; or a captured Photo — and can convert back out to bytes, a data URL, a PIL image, or a saved file. Manipulation methods (resize, rotate, crop, ...) each return a new Picture, and two Pictures are == when their pixels match, so Pictures stored in state work naturally with assert_equal.

    URL-backed Pictures are lazy: Picture("https://.../dog.png") does not fetch anything until the pixels are first needed, so handing one to the Image component just uses the URL directly.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    filename str | None

    Original upload/file name, if any.
    mime_type str

    The image's MIME type; sniffed or provided, defaulting to image/png.

    Build a Picture from any supported image source.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    source

    A path, URL, or data URL string; bytes/bytearray; a PIL image; another Picture (copied); an uploaded DrafterBinaryFile; or a captured Photo.

    		 required
    filename str | None

    Optional filename to record as metadata.

    		 None
    mime_type str | None

    Optional MIME type override.

    		 None

    Raises:

    Type Description
    StudentFacingError

    If the source is not a supported type, or its data cannot be decoded as an image.

    height property

    Height of the image in pixels.

    url property

    The backing URL for a URL-sourced Picture, or None.

    Set only while the Picture's pixels are byte-identical to what the URL serves (manipulations return new Pictures without it), so it is always safe to display the URL instead of the pixels.

    width property

    Width of the image in pixels.

    __copy__()

    Copy the picture (pixels are duplicated, metadata kept).

    __deepcopy__(memo)

    Deep-copy the picture; unloaded URL sources stay unloaded.

    __eq__(other)

    Compare by pixels (mode, size, and raw data); metadata such as the filename is intentionally ignored.

    __repr__()

    Short form like Picture('dog.png', 640x480, PNG) — never a base64 dump.

    crop(left, top, right, bottom)

    A new Picture cut down to the box from (left, top) to (right, bottom).

    flip_horizontal()

    A new Picture mirrored left-to-right.

    flip_vertical()

    A new Picture mirrored top-to-bottom.

    Redirect(target_route, state_update=None, **kwargs) dataclass

    Bases: ResponsePayload

    A Redirect is a payload that will redirect the user to a new route.

    Often, it is simpler to simply call a different route function inline. However, that will not change the back/forward history of the browser. A Redirect payload will cause the browser to navigate to a new route, updating the history as appropriate. In other words, this is like a proper version of a function call that the client is aware of.

    RemovePersistent(target, **kwargs) dataclass

    Bases: Component

    Removes a persisted component when this page is rendered.

    Renders as an invisible marker element; when the page loads, the persisted component whose key matches target is stopped and discarded. If no matching component is currently persisted, nothing happens.

    The target can be identified three ways:

    • The id the persistent component was created with (recommended): RemovePersistent("background-music")
    • An equivalent component instance (same constructor arguments): RemovePersistent(Audio("theme.mp3", persistent=True))
    • A raw derived key string (shown in the debug panel's Persisted list).

    add_website_css_file(path, server=None)

    Adds a CSS file to every page.

    path may be the path to a CSS file next to the student's program, or a full URL to a stylesheet.

    A file next to the program is checked right away: if it cannot be found, a friendly error explains where Drafter looked and suggests similarly named files. The file is also registered like add_website_file, so it travels with the site when it is built.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    path str

    The path of a .css file next to your program (such as "style.css" or "static/style.css"), or a full URL.

    		 required
    server ClientServer | None

    The server to configure. If None, uses the main server.

    		 None

    Raises:

    Type Description
    StudentFacingError

    If the path is not a string, looks like CSS code rather than a file name, is not a .css file, or cannot be found.

    Registers files next to the student's program as part of the website, so that they are copied into the built site when it is deployed.

    Use this for files the site needs at runtime (data files that are open()ed, images, fonts, and so on). Each file is checked right away; a missing file raises a friendly error that suggests similarly named files.

    Type Description

    quiet bool

    Suppress the printed SUCCESS message when the test passes.

    Returns:

    Name Type Description
    bool bool

    True if the text matched, False otherwise.

    open(file_path, mode='r', *args, **kwargs)

    Opens files for reading or writing, with special handling for web environments.

    This is Drafter's replacement for the built-in open (it is installed over builtins.open when this module is imported), abstracting away differences between running in a web context and a standard Python environment. In Pyodide, relative paths resolve inside the current instance's virtual folder, and files missing from the virtual filesystem are fetched over HTTP relative to the page URL. Outside the web, http:///https:// paths are downloaded and returned as in-memory file objects, and relative paths resolve against the configured user directory (or the current working directory).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    file_path

    The path to the file to open. In a web environment, this may be a virtual path resolved inside the instance's folder; it may also be an http:// or https:// URL.

    		 required
    mode

    The mode in which to open the file (e.g., "r" for read, "w" for write). Defaults to "r".

    		 'r'
    *args

    Additional positional arguments passed through to the underlying built-in open.

    		 ()
    **kwargs

    Additional keyword arguments passed through to the underlying built-in open (e.g., encoding).

    		 {}

    Returns:

    Type Description

    A file-like object for reading from or writing to the given path, with behavior adapted to the execution environment.

    Raises:

    Type Description
    ValueError

    If file_path is not a string, pathlib.Path, or os.PathLike.
    FileNotFoundError

    If the file cannot be found locally or fetched over HTTP.

    set_browser_history(enabled=True, server=None)

    Enables or disables mirroring navigation into the browser's history stack. When enabled (the default for standalone sites), the browser's back/forward buttons time travel through the app, restoring each page's state. When disabled, Drafter never touches the browser's history or URL, so the back button leaves the page — the right behavior for an app embedded in another page (documentation demos disable it automatically).

    Call before start_server(); the setting is read when the site boots.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    enabled bool

    Whether to mirror navigation into browser history.

    		 True
    server ClientServer | None

    The server to configure. If None, uses the main server.

    		 None

    set_page_transition(transition='fade', duration=None, server=None)

    Sets a site-wide visual transition that plays whenever the user navigates between pages. By default, pages change instantly; this setting makes the new page fade in instead.

    The transition can be:

    • "fade" (or "transparent"): the new page fades in from transparent.
    • A CSS color such as "black", "white", or "#004488": the new page fades in from a solid veil of that color.
    • "none" (or None): disables the transition again.

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    transition str | None

    The transition style ("fade", "none", or a CSS color).

    		 'fade'
    duration float | None

    How long the transition lasts, in seconds. If not given, the current duration (0.5 seconds by default) is kept.

    		 None
    server ClientServer | None

    The server to configure. If None, uses the main server.

    		 None

    start_server(initial_state=None, server=None, server_name=None, in_debug_mode=None, framed=None, theme=None, site_title=None, favicon=None, information=None, verbose=None, asset_directory=None, show_filename_as=None, engine=None, port=None, host=None, prerender_initial_page=None, open_browser=None, browser=None, inline_py=None, use_reloader=None, pyodide_url=None, pyodide_version=None, pyodide_branch=None, reloader=None, cdn_skulpt=None, cdn_skulpt_std=None, cdn_skulpt_drafter=None, skip=None, argv=None, **extra_configuration)

    Start the Drafter server (web or local development mode).

    Routes to either ClientServer (web mode) or AppServer (local dev mode) based on execution context. In web mode, initializes browser-side bridge; in local mode, starts Starlette dev server with file watching.

    This function is the primary entry point for users and accepts parameters for both ClientServer and AppServer modes (the appropriate ones are used depending on context).

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    initial_state

    Optional initial application state.

    		 None
    server

    Optional pre-created server instance (defaults to main server).

    		 None
    server_name str | None

    Server identifier name.

    		 None
    in_debug_mode bool | None

    Enable debug panel and logging.

    		 None
    framed bool | None

    Whether to frame the content.

    		 None
    theme str | None

    Theme name (e.g., "default").

    		 None
    site_title str | None

    Title displayed in UI.

    		 None
    favicon str | None

    Browser tab icon: a URL or the path to an adjacent image file (svg, png, ico, ...).

    		 None
    information dict | None

    Dict of site information (author, description, etc.).

    		 None
    verbose bool | None

    Enable verbose logging.

    		 None
    asset_directory MaybeBoolStr

    Assets directory (uses Drafter defaults if False).

    		 None
    show_filename_as MaybeBoolStr

    Display filename in UI (if different from actual).

    		 None
    engine EngineType | None

    Python engine ("skulpt" or "pyodide").

    		 None
    port int | None

    Server port for dev mode.

    		 None
    host str | None

    Server host for dev mode.

    		 None
    prerender_initial_page bool | None

    Prerender initial page on startup.

    		 None
    open_browser bool | None

    Auto-open browser in dev mode.

    		 None
    browser str | None

    Which browser to open in dev mode: "chrome", "firefox", "safari", "edge", or "default" for the system default. When not given, Chrome is used if installed, then Firefox, then the system default.

    		 None
    inline_py bool | None

    Inline code in HTML vs. load via HTTP.

    		 None
    use_reloader bool | None

    Enable file watcher and auto-reload.

    		 None
    pyodide_url str | None

    Base URL to load Pyodide from (default: jsDelivr CDN).

    		 None
    pyodide_version str | None

    Pyodide version segment, e.g. "v314.0.5" or "dev".

    		 None
    pyodide_branch str | None

    Pyodide distribution branch, "full" or "debug".

    		 None
    reloader bool | None

    Deprecated alias for use_reloader, kept for compatibility with older versions; used only when use_reloader is not given.

    		 None
    cdn_skulpt str | None

    Deprecated and ignored; passing a value prints a warning.

    		 None
    cdn_skulpt_std str | None

    Deprecated and ignored; passing a value prints a warning.

    		 None
    cdn_skulpt_drafter str | None

    Deprecated and ignored; passing a value prints a warning.

    		 None
    skip bool | None

    If True, do nothing at all — do not start the server or compile anything. Useful for running unit tests against a site file. Also settable via the DRAFTER_SKIP environment variable, the --skip flag, or a config file.

    		 None
    argv list[str] | None

    Command-line argument override passed into the system configuration.

    		 None
    **extra_configuration

    Additional configuration parameters.

    		 {}

    Raises:

    Type Description
    SystemExit

    In local development mode, when the server cannot start for a reason that has a student-facing explanation (the main file is missing, the port is in use). The explanation is printed instead of a traceback; with the verbose setting on, the original StudentFacingError propagates instead.

    Updates the attribute of a component, returning the component (allowing you to chain calls). The attr property should match the HTML attribute name.

    Example attributes include: - id - class - title

    Parameters:

    Name Type Description Default
    component PageContent

    The component to update. May also be a plain value (a string, number, or boolean, which is wrapped in a new Text component) or a list of components (each element is updated).

    		 required
    attr str

    The name of the attribute to change

    		 required
    value str

    The value to set the attribute to (should be a string).

    		 required

    Returns:

    Type Description
    Component | list[Component]

    The updated component. If a component was given, the original component is updated in place and returned. If a plain value was given, a new Text component wrapping it is returned. If a list was given, a new list of the updated elements is returned.
